chunks: Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Ya'qub who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Three things are such that people cannot [easily] bear them: pardoning [the wrongs of] others, assisting someone [else] with one’s wealth, and remembering Allah often.'

Ibn Abi Ya'qub said: 'Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Whoever speaks regarding [a matter pertaining to] justice yet goes against it [himself] to something else, he shall be burdened with [great] regret on the Day of Resurrection.'
ai.seo_question: What are the three difficult virtues mentioned by Imam al-Sadiq and the consequence of hypocrisy in justice?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights three arduous yet essential virtues: pardoning others, sharing wealth, and frequent remembrance of God. Ibn Abi Ya'qub adds that hypocrisy in justice—preaching it while acting contrary to it—leads to regret on the Day of Judgment. This hadith, found in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the Shia emphasis on aligning inner conviction with outward action, a key theme in ethical jurisprudence.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 15.Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from Durust, from Abū Salamah, from Abū Yaʿqūb who said, “Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘Three things are such that people cannot [easily] bear them: pardoning [the wrongs of] others, assisting someone [else] with one’s wealth, and remembering Allah often.’” Ibn Abī Yaʿqūb said, “Abū ʿAbdillāh (a) said, ‘Whoever speaks regarding [a matter pertaining to] justice yet goes against it [himself] to something else, he shall be burdened with [great] regret on the Day of Resurrection.’”
